functions.name: InitializeCelContextInfo
functions.comment:
Initialize cel context information for D2 graphics rendering

Algorithm:
1. Extract component index from unit structure at offset +0x1d
2. Copy unit type, unit ID, and class ID from source unit to cel context
3. Lookup component type from global table using component index
4. Lookup weapon class from global table using unit class ID  
5. Lookup unit type info from global table using unit type
6. Set default cel file name to 'lit ' (0x2074696c)
7. Check for custom cel file override in unit component array
8. Validate COF data pointer exists in unit structure at +0xb8
9. Call FUN_10001c20 to get COF data with dimensions and cel file info
10. Loop through COF component entries to find matching component
11. Check component index bounds (must be < 16, validate with 0xf)
12. When matching component found, set animation direction flags
13. Extract 4-byte cel file name from COF component data
14. Replace null bytes in cel file name with space (0x20) for padding
15. Validate all required context fields are non-zero before return
16. Set default values for missing cel file and component flags

Parameters:
pUnit (int*): Pointer to unit structure containing type, ID, class, and component data
pCelContext (int*): Output cel context structure to populate with rendering info

Returns:
void: Function terminates with FUN_100149f1(-1) on validation failures

Special Cases:
- Animation direction: Set to 0 if unit type < 5, otherwise set to 1
- Missing cel file override: Uses default 'lit ' name (0x2074696c)
- Null bytes in cel file: Replaced with space character (0x20)
- Missing component/weapon class: Set to default 'xxx ' (0x20787878)
- Validation failures: Call error logging then terminate process

Magic Numbers:
0x1d - Component index offset in unit structure
0x24, 0x28 - Unit type and ID offsets in cel context  
0x34, 0x38, 0x3c, 0x40 - Component info offsets in cel context
0xb8 - COF data pointer offset in unit structure
0x2074696c - Default 'lit ' cel file name
0x20787878 - Default 'xxx ' component name  
0xf - Maximum component index (16 components: 0-15)
0x5 - Animation direction threshold for unit types

Structure Layout:
Unit Structure:
Offset | Size | Field Name    | Type  | Description
+0x1c  | 4    | dwUnitType   | uint  | Unit type identifier
+0x1d  | 1    | bComponent   | byte  | Component index for this unit
+0x20  | 4    | dwUnitId     | uint  | Unique unit identifier
+0x24  | 4    | dwClassId    | uint  | Unit class/subtype
+0x38  | 64   | celOverrides | uint[16] | Custom cel file overrides by component
+0xb8  | 4    | pCofData     | void* | Pointer to COF animation data

Cel Context Structure:
Offset | Size | Field Name        | Type  | Description  
+0x1d  | 1    | bComponent       | byte  | Component index
+0x20  | 4    | dwFlags          | uint  | Animation direction flags
+0x24  | 4    | dwUnitType      | uint  | Unit type identifier
+0x28  | 4    | dwUnitId        | uint  | Unique unit identifier  
+0x30  | 4    | dwUnitToType    | uint  | Unit type lookup value
+0x34  | 4    | dwComponentType | uint  | Component type from table
+0x38  | 4    | dwCelFile       | uint  | 4-char cel file name
+0x3c  | 4    | dwWClass        | uint  | Weapon class identifier
+0x40  | 4    | dwComponentFlags| uint  | Component-specific flags

functions.name: ProcessCompositeUnitGraphics
functions.comment:
Processes and renders composite unit graphics components.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input composite unit pointer for null
2. Check unit visibility flags using gdwBitMasks_exref bitmasks
3. Extract base width (field 5) and height (field 6) from composite unit
4. Validate graphics info pointer at offset 0x2e exists
5. Iterate through graphics info linked list to find matching frame
6. Match by animation type (field 8) and direction lookup (field 9)
7. Validate COF (Component Object File) data pointer exists
8. Extract frame position from unit coordinates (field 1 & 2)
9. Calculate frame data offset using COF header and position
10. First pass: count valid components and calculate maximum width
11. For each component in COF data validate component type < 16
12. Initialize component structure with unit reference and coordinates
13. Call thunk_FUN_10001960 to set up component rendering context
14. Call Ordinal_10055 to prepare component for rendering
15. Call Ordinal_10040 to get component width and update maximum
16. Second pass: render all components if count > 0
17. For each component call Ordinal_10079 to perform actual rendering

Parameters:
pCompositeUnit (uint*): Pointer to composite unit structure containing:
  Field 0: Visibility flags
  Field 1: X coordinate (byte)
  Field 2: Y coordinate with direction in upper bits
  Field 5: Base width
  Field 6: Base height 
  Field 8: Animation type identifier
  Field 9: Direction index for lookup table
  Field 0x2e: Pointer to graphics info linked list

Returns:
void - No return value, performs rendering side effects

Special Cases:
- Null pointer validation with assertion and exit(-1)
- Missing graphics info assertion and exit(-1)
- Missing COF data assertion and exit(-1)
- Component type >= 16 assertion and exit(-1)
- Empty COF (no components) returns immediately
- Zero valid components returns without rendering

Error Handling:
All error conditions trigger Ordinal_10021 assertion with source file and line
followed by FUN_100149f1(0xffffffff) which exits the process

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x44e - Line number for null unit pointer check
0x45e - Line number for null graphics info check  
0x466 - Line number for null COF data check
0x2ad - Line number for null frame data check
0x429 - Line number for invalid component type check
0x475 - Line number for component type check in render loop
0x2e - Offset to graphics info pointer in composite unit
0x14 - Offset to COF data in graphics info node
0x1c - COF header size before component data

functions.name: InitializeColorPalettes
functions.comment:
Initialize color palette conversion arrays by processing RGB source data

Algorithm:

1. Initialize first loop: Set index to 0, point to source palette 1 at 0x10026c79
2. Process first RGB array: For each 3-byte RGB triplet in source palette 1:
   a. Extract RGB components: red (ESI-1), green (ESI), blue (ESI+1)  
   b. Call color conversion function Ordinal_10030(red, green, blue)
   c. Store returned byte value in g_abProcessedPalette1[index]
   d. Advance pointer by 3 bytes to next RGB triplet
   e. Increment index counter
   f. Continue until pointer reaches end boundary 0x10026c97
3. Reset for second palette: Set index to 0, point to source palette 2 at 0x10026c99
4. Process second RGB array: Identical process as step 2 but:
   a. Source data from g_SourcePalette2 (0x10026c99 to 0x10026cb7)
   b. Output stored in g_abProcessedPalette2 array at 0x10065f50

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void - No return value (initialization function)

Special Cases:
Loop boundaries are hardcoded memory addresses ensuring exact palette sizes
First palette: 10 RGB entries (0x10026c79 to 0x10026c97, 30 bytes / 3 = 10)
Second palette: 10 RGB entries (0x10026c99 to 0x10026cb7, 30 bytes / 3 = 10)

Structure Layout:
RGBColor (3 bytes):
Offset  Size  Field   Type   Description
0x0     1     red     byte   Red color component (0-255)
0x1     1     green   byte   Green color component (0-255) 
0x2     1     blue    byte   Blue color component (0-255)

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x10026c79 - Start of source palette 1 RGB data
0x10026c97 - End boundary for source palette 1 (exclusive)
0x10026c99 - Start of source palette 2 RGB data  
0x10026cb7 - End boundary for source palette 2 (exclusive)
0x10065f5c - Output array for processed palette 1
0x10065f50 - Output array for processed palette 2
0x3 - RGB triplet stride (3 bytes per color)
